tweets.text:
The biggest issue with an AI "safety slowdown:"

What happens with China?

While there are legitimate concerns around the safety of AI and how quickly it is evolving, the AI race is global.

And, in today's ecosystem, falling even 6 months behind in the AI race is like falling decades behind in the pre-AI world.

If US AI giants agree to slow progress and focus on safety, there must be an international agreement in place as well.

And, even if there is an agreement in place, how do we regulate compliance?

We've said it before and we will say it again: AI is the biggest technological revolution in history.

This is an AI arms race that may be impossible to fully regulate.

tweets.text:
Bloomberg says Europe's energy squeeze is a signal of 'rising interest rates.' That is exactly backwards.

European natural gas is back above €70 a megawatt-hour, the highest since March and roughly double the summer, though still far below the 2022 crisis peak near €340. At the same time Europe's diesel crack spread just hit a record. Diesel has never been this expensive relative to crude.

This is a physical supply squeeze heading into winter, not a monetary event. Cold weather and tight refineries do not expand the money supply.

A rate hike does not produce a molecule of gas or a barrel of diesel. It just raises the cost of the loans people use to pay the bill. When energy spikes, the honest word is supply shock, not inflation. Hiking into it would punish the economy for a problem the Fed did not cause and cannot fix.

Something broke in the French bond market. Safe bank bonds now yield less than the French government.

The spread just hit a record low. 10-year French covered bonds, the collateralized debt banks issue against pools of mortgages, now yield less than 10-year French government bonds. The market prices a segregated pool of home loans as safer than the French state.

The reason is fiscal. France is running debt at 117% of GDP with a record €310 billion of new bond sales planned for 2026, and its 10-year spread over Germany just hit 90 basis points, the widest since 2012.

When a government's own bonds trade cheaper than the banks it backstops, the balance sheet is the risk. Bond markets discipline governments long before voters do.

tweets.text:
The average 30-year mortgage is back near 6.6%, and the Fed cannot wave it down.

Mortgage rates track the 10-year Treasury, not the Fed funds rate. That is why they ripped from 2.8% in 2022 to almost 8%, then got stuck in the 6s no matter what the Fed did.

The one lever you actually control is the lender's margin. Your rate has a profit cushion baked in. Get a written quote from a second lender and take it back to your first, and ask them to match or beat it. In the Journal's example, a 6.625% quote used against a 6.875% one.

A quarter point on a $400,000 loan is about $66 a month and roughly $24,000 over the life of the loan. No rate cut from Washington required.

tweets.text:
The resale market is a lie detector for luxury.

A Rolex holds about 100% of its sticker price on resale. Wear it for years, sell it for roughly what you paid. A Hermès watch keeps 41%, down from 51% four years ago. Louis Vuitton keeps 35%.

Here is the tell. The Journal reports that many buyers get Hermès watches to build spending history and improve their odds of being allowed to buy a Birkin bag, then resell the watch. That is why it can lose almost 60% the moment it leaves the store.

Resale value is the market pricing real demand. Rolex is a store of value. Most luxury is depreciating consumption wearing an investment costume.

A company with zero data-center revenue wants a $50 billion valuation.

SB Energy has no data centers running and lost $3.2 billion in the first half of 2026. Its pitch is one chart: expected revenue where almost nothing lands in the next two years, and the biggest bar, hundreds of billions of dollars, sits 8 or more years out.

To build it, the company needs over $170 billion of capital. Its anchor customer is OpenAI, which SB Energy lists in its own filing as a risk to that revenue.

This is the AI trade in one picture. Pay for the hype today. Collect the cash next decade, if it shows up.
